subject: HealthBridge security questionnaire: access roles & dataflow diagram
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@healthbridge.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@healthbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security questionnaire: DFD + access role clarifications

Hi Lauren / Connor,

Thanks again for the quick kickoff yesterday. Our security team is finishing the vendor intake and had two focused asks we hoped you could answer this week: a) a high-level data flow diagram that shows where PII travels (ingest, transient caches, storage, metrics), and b) a concise access-role matrix that explains which Redwood teams/systems can access PII at rest and in transit.

Specifically, our SSQ calls out:
- Token-level logs retention and whether any raw PII is present in telemetry
- Who (by role) can retrieve persisted request payloads and for what reasons
- Cross-border transfer routes and any anonymization/pseudonymization applied at ingest

Can you provide a DFD and the access matrix (or point us to the artifact)? If you have a short note about encryption in transit and at rest for the token payloads that would be great. We have a compliance deadline on Friday 10/23.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Security Operations
HealthBridge

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: DFD + access role clarifications

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. See answers below and attached artifacts.

Quick bullets first:
- We attached a high-level DFD (redwood-dfd-v1.pdf) that highlights four zones: Ingest Edge, Processing (LLM runtime + KV cache), Persistent Storage (encrypted object store), and Observability (telemetry backend). PII flows only through Ingest -> Processing. Persistent Storage stores pseudonymized request IDs and labeled artifacts; we do not persist raw user text by default unless retention is requested.
- Access matrix attached (healthbridge-access-matrix.csv): maps roles (SRE, Platform Eng, Inference Ops, Support) to actions (read payloads, view logs, export artifacts). Short summary:
  - Support: can view anonymized request metadata only; cannot retrieve raw payloads
  - Inference Ops: can access runtime traces and KV cache snapshots for debugging; access to full payloads is gated and logged; requires approval from two engineers + ticket attached to Jira SUP-9876
  - SRE/Platform Eng: can access infra-level logs and telemetry; tokenized PII removed from those logs by default

Encryption notes (short):
- In transit: TLS1.3 enforced between customer -> edge -> internal services.
- At rest: AES-256 for object stores and KMS for key management. Customer-managed KMS is available for Private deployments; hosted customers use Redwood KMS by default.

Attachments: redwood-dfd-v1.pdf (high-level PDF), healthbridge-access-matrix.csv (CSV role map). Also adding a Drive folder link for the evidence bundle: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-HealthBridge-SSQ

If you'd like, Connor and Marissa can join a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow morning to step through the DFD and the gating workflow for payload retrieval.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Privacy & Trust (interim)
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: DFD + access role clarifications

Lauren — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple follow-ups from our security reviewer:

1) The DFD shows a "KV cache" in Processing. Can you confirm whether unredacted user inputs can appear in cache snapshots that are persisted for debugging? If so, what's the retention and who can extract snapshots?

2) In your access matrix the Inference Ops row says "gated and logged" — can you point to the ticketing workflow (Jira or internal runbook) and the minimum approvers required? Our compliance team requires two distinct approvers for payload retrieval.

3) Can you confirm whether any telemetry exports to third-party observability services include sample request text (even if pseudonymized)? We specifically need assurance that exported telemetry is free of raw PII.

If you can reply by EOD tomorrow (Thu 10/22) that would keep us on schedule.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Vendor Risk
HealthBridge

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@healthbridge.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@healthbridge.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Patel <m.patel@cybersecure.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: DFD + access role clarifications

Tom / Samantha — thanks for the follow-ups. Answers inline below.

1) KV cache persistence:
- Short answer: unredacted user inputs can appear in in-memory KV state during active inference, but snapshots persisted to disk are pseudonymized by default. We retain persisted snapshots only for debugging on a per-request basis and only when a retention flag is set by an ops ticket. Default retention window for persisted snapshots is 7 days, configurable per-customer.
- Extraction policy: only Inference Ops staff with two-step approval (one Inference Ops engineer + an on-call Platform Eng) can extract a snapshot; every extraction is recorded with the ticket ID and signed log entries. Example: Jira SUP-9876 records the approval chain and extraction artifact.

2) Ticketing workflow and approvers:
- Workflow: create a Jira SUP ticket with justification -> assign to Inference Ops -> first approval by an Inference Ops senior engineer -> second approval by Platform Eng on-call -> engineering manager final sign-off for any retention beyond 7 days. All steps are required for payload retrieval. We included a sanitized runbook excerpt in the Drive folder (see related link).

3) Telemetry exports:
- We do not export raw request text to third-party observability services by default. Exported telemetry contains hashed/pseudonymized request identifiers and aggregate metrics only. Raw payloads are kept in our object store and are not part of telemetry export pipelines. Customers using Private deployments can opt to route telemetry to customer-owned endpoints.

Next steps:
- I've uploaded the sanitized runbook and an excerpt of the Jira approval template to the Drive folder.
- If HealthBridge would like an attestation, we can provide a scoped statement for the SSQ items above and include it in the onboarding evidence bundle.

Happy to schedule the walkthrough tomorrow 9:00am PT if that works for your team.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
